completed_episode_note: each pair replans twice (one ASSIGNMENT per failure); the FIRST episode is interrupted by the second failure detection before any transfer completes, so its two-impulse bound is the cost of COMPLETING the commanded transfer within the truncated window -- a continuous partial burn need not pay that, which is why whole-run totals can sit below it (ratio_total < 1). The FINAL episode ends at RECOVERED: same start state, target slot and transfer time as an actual completed transfer, so its spend-vs-bound ratio is the apples-to-apples figure.

g4_headline_pair_1_2.note: two_failure.json == P0 pair (1,2) (failures: sat 1 at t=1200, sat 2 at t=1500; GATES.md P0 row's pair_1-2__hungarian.jsonl is the same run); its worst sat and totals, for direct comparison with the G4 single-run ledger row (GATES.md G4: per-sat dv 0-193.68 m/s at a_max = 0.1)

headline.definition: the G4 headline per-satellite dv (193.68 m/s, GATES.md G4 row, reproduced as the worst sat's dv_used in P0 pairs (1,2) (1,3) (1,4) (1,5) (3,4) (3,5), and as sat 0's total also in (4,5) where sat 2 is the worst sat) divided by the same satellite's two-impulse CW bound for its ACTUAL COMPLETED transfer (final episode: start state at the final replan tick, assigned slot, window replan tick -> RECOVERED tick)

method: two-impulse CW transfer from the hcw STM velocity block (cubesat.hcw.stm), same start state (REPLANNING tick), target slot (ASSIGNMENT event, slot_initial_state reconstruction of allocate.select_formation) and transfer time (replan tick -> next FAILURE_DETECTED or RECOVERED tick) as the actual run; ENDGAME_PLAN section 2 resolution method, post-hoc, zero core diff
